messages:
Anna Li: Heads up — I see a regression on the paged-attention memory-bandwidth path after yesterday's runtime push. 95p latency for seq=2048 jumped ~1.7x on T4. nvprof/nsys shows a lot more STALL_MEMORY and lower sustained GB/s.

Josh Park: Which commit / change did you suspect? Can you paste the nvprof output + model details (seq, batch, model)?

Anna Li: seq=2048, batch=1, model=redwood/attn-test. Kernel: flash_paged_v3 (the new tiled prefetch path). Quick nvprof snippet: 
```
== PROFILES ==
Kernel: flash_paged_v3  Launch: (grid=1024, block=128)  smem=49152
GPU Mem BW (measured): 120 GB/s  (expected ~240-260 GB/s)
sm_efficiency: 0.28  stall_reasons: STALL_MEMORY 42%
Previous kernel (flash_paged_v2): GPU Mem BW: 245 GB/s  stall_reasons: OTHER 12%
```

Maria Gomez: That smells like tiling/pipeline reorder that reduces coalesced loads or increases serialization. I recently merged the sharedmem-prefetch change (PR #1769) which changed stage ordering — could affect global load patterns and occupancy.

Josh Park: I ran the same workload on an A100 quickly — no regression there. So this is arch-sensitive (T4 memory subsystem / L2 behavior / wmma vs. tensor core not involved). Can you dump the kernel launch params + occupancy numbers?

Anna Li: Paste of kernel params: 
```
Kernel: flash_paged_v3
gridDim: 1024
blockDim: 128
sharedMem: 49152 bytes
regs_per_thread: 64
theoretical_occupancy: 0.5
measured_occupancy: 0.34
```
Measured occupancy dropped compared to v2 (0.75 -> 0.34). Also see increased L2 misses in the trace.

Kevin Zhou: Noticed KV-cache miss rate increased in request traces around the same deploy window — cold-start miss ratio up ~15%. If kernel is thrashing SMEM or changing prefix cache locality patterns, it could amplify memory BW.

Anna Li: I rolled back the sharedmem-prefetch locally and perf returned to baseline on T4. So it's likely tied to that change. I'll bisect next.

ops-bot: [deploy] canary deployed to cluster:edge-t4-1 (tag: runtime-2026-11-08).

Maria Gomez: Plan: 1) Bisect commits around the smem-prefetch and batching-router changes; 2) Add per-kernel mem-bandwidth counters (nsys sampling) in the runtime debug build; 3) Emit lightweight sampling (1%) of kernel launch params + occupancy for seq>1024 in prod so we can correlate across hardware. I'll open a PR with diagnostic flags.

Kevin Zhou: I'll add a canary routing rule to pin a small percentage of traffic to T4 fleet for regression repro (+1% sampling for seq>1024). Also will disable the new eviction heuristic in the KV cache for that canary to separate effects. :thumbsup:

Josh Park: Sounds good. If bisect confirms smem-prefetch is the culprit we should consider fallback to v2 tiling on low-bandwidth GPUs (detect via measured sustained GB/s). I can sketch a fallback policy in the runtime router.

Anna Li: Cool — starting bisect now. Will post the first failing commit and a minimal repro once found. Thanks all.
